key_insight: The paper shows that open models can sometimes act as faithful surrogates for closed models, but only under specific conditions and at different levels of analysis. For binary classification, API-accessible log-odds can serve as a useful bridge for interpreting closed-model behavior.
problem_solved: Mechanistic interpretability usually needs full access to model internals, but most deployed LLMs only expose limited API outputs. This paper addresses the surrogate problem: when can measurements from an open model legitimately support claims about a closed model?
method: Evaluate surrogate fidelity at three levels: prediction, attribution, and representation.
Use open-model measurements to test how well they match closed-model behavior under API-like constraints.
Focus on binary classification settings where log-odds provide an accessible scalar readout.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners understand when interpretability studies on open models can transfer to proprietary systems. It provides a practical framework for deciding which insights are trustworthy when only limited model access is available.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline showing open model analysis vs closed model API access

paper_title: Surrogate Fidelity: When Can Open LLMs Explain Closed Ones?
paper_authors: Philippe Chlenski, Zachariah Carmichael, Ayush Warikoo, Chia-Tse Shao, Yingxiao Ye
